title: Application of VHH-immobilized cryogel-based immunoaffinity chromatography for isolation of extracellular vesicles from human plasma
projectDescription: Proteomics profiles of extracellular vesicles isolated using a new cryogel-based immunoaffinity chromatography system functionalized with single-domain VHH antibodies for selective isolation of EVs from human plasma.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Extracellular Vesicles in suspension (4 μg of protein) underwent protein precipitation using six volumes of acetone, followed by centrifugation at 18,200 RCF. Reduction and alkylation were performed using TCEP/CAA, followed by trypsin digestion. Peptides were purified using C18 stage tips before LC-MS/MS analysis. Stage tips were conditioned with 250 μL of MeCN, 250 μL of elution solvent (40% MeCN with 0.5% acetic acid) followed by 250 μL of solvent A (H₂O with 0.5% acetic acid). Peptides were loaded and washed with solvent A, and final elution was performed with 40 μL of elution solvent, then dried, reconstituted in solvent A, and injected for LC-MS/MS analysis.
dataProcessingProtocol: The raw data were analyzed using FragPipe v23.0,  using quantification with DIA-NN v2.0.0, in library-free mode. DIA-Tracer was used to enhance feature alignment and quantification consistency across runs. The search included a tolerance for up to four missed cleavages, peptide length ranging from 5 to 30 amino acids and peptide mass ranging from 300 to 5,000 Da. The false discovery rate (FDR) was set to 1%. Data were queried against UP000005640 and UP000001509 (the latter to verify the absence of remaining E. coli proteins).
